Jake (Acme): Hey team — our March invoice INV-2026-0319 is showing ~1,200,312 tokens but the usage dashboard for org acme-prod shows 320,874 for the same period. We're being charged ~$1,420 more than expected. Can someone help reconcile?

Alice (Support): Sorry about that, Jake. Can you confirm the account/org id and the API key prefix you used? Also did you export any CSVs that you can attach? :eyes:

Jake (Acme): org: `acme-prod`
API key prefix: `rk_live_ABC`
I attached a tiny CSV in the ticket but here's the curl we use for bulk requests:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_live_ABC" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3-large","input":"...","max_tokens":512}'
```
We also do retries from our worker when requests timeout (simple exponential backoff).

Alice (Support): Thanks. Two quick checks: (1) are your retries idempotent (do you set a `request_id` header)? (2) can you share a sample `request_id` if you have one? Dashboard dedupe usually uses `request_id` if present.

Jake (Acme): We don't set a `request_id` header — retries just replay the same payload. Sample trace from our side: `worker-20260319-7f2`: request started 2026-03-19T14:02:11Z, timed out at 14:02:20Z, retried and succeeded 14:02:28Z.

Raj (EngOps): I'm pulling billing logs now. Preliminary: invoice aggregator and dashboard use different dedupe heuristics. Dashboard dedupes by payload hash + `request_id` when present; aggregator was deduping by `request_id` only. If no `request_id` we ended up counting both attempts in the invoice.

Raj (EngOps): Example from the billing stream:```json
{
  "event_type":"token_counted",
  "timestamp":"2026-03-19T14:02:28Z",
  "request_id":null,
  "payload_hash":"3f8a9c...",
  "batch_id":"b-9981",
  "tokens":512
}
{
  "event_type":"token_counted",
  "timestamp":"2026-03-19T14:02:11Z",
  "request_id":null,
  "payload_hash":"3f8a9c...",
  "batch_id":"b-9979",
  "tokens":512
}
```
Both events were counted by the invoice pipeline. Dashboard merged them because it computed the same `payload_hash`. That's the root cause.

Alice (Support): Thanks Raj. Do we have a quick workaround for customers who don't set `request_id`? I can ask Acme to enable idempotency headers but they may not want to deploy a change immediately.

Raj (EngOps): Short-term: we can backfill adjustments for affected invoices. Long-term: we'll update the invoice aggregator to dedupe by payload_hash when `request_id` is null (safe fix). I've already created ENG-5143 to track the aggregator change.

Maya (Finance): Flagging for revrec: if we issue a credit we need to record a contra revenue entry and include the adjustment reason `metering_dup_count_correction`. Please provide a list of the affected invoice lines and the net credit amount.

Raj (EngOps): I ran a scan for `acme-prod` between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-31. Duplicate-counted tokens: 279,438 tokens. Using your hosted pricing tier that equates to $142.30. I can export per-request rows.

Maya (Finance): Perfect. Please attach the CSV with columns: `invoice_id`,`line_item_id`,`original_tokens`,`dedup_tokens`,`credit_amount`. We'll create adjustment INV-2026-0319-ADJ and issue a negative invoice/credit memo. Also need GL code and revrec memo text. Use `REVREC: Billing correction for duplicate token counts (dashboard vs invoice) - acme-prod`.

Alice (Support): Jake — we will issue a credit for $142.30 and create INV-2026-0319-ADJ. You'll see a credit memo in ~24-48hrs. Sorry again for the noise. :pray: Would you be able to implement an idempotency header within the next sprint? That will prevent this class of issue.

Jake (Acme): Thanks, Alice and team. We can add a `x-request-id` header starting next week. For now, the credit fixes our billing dispute. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

billing-bot: Created ticket FIN-8672 for adjustment and linked ENG-5143.

Maya (Finance): Adjustment created: INV-2026-0319-ADJ, credit amount: $142.30, posting date: 2026-04-02. Revrec note: `REVREC: Billing correction for duplicate token counts (dashboard vs invoice) - acme-prod`. We'll mark the original invoice as partially adjusted.

Raj (EngOps): Deploy plan for aggregator fix: 1) add payload_hash dedupe when `request_id` is null, 2) run backfill test on staging, 3) rollout canary for 24h, 4) full rollout. ETA: patch next week, canary in 3 business days.

Alice (Support): Closing loop here — credit issued and ENG fix scheduled. Jake, reopen if you see any other delta. :thumbsup:

Jake (Acme): All good, thanks again.

Alice (Support): Closing thread. Adding `metering-billing-adjustment` tag for records.
